files.modifications: none (byte-identical to the upstream v3.11.3 release asset)
digest_cross_checks: https://github.com/nlohmann/json/discussions/4223 (official v3.11.3 release announcement publishes the same SHA-256)
files.notice_obligation: retain the upstream MIT SPDX header in the vendored file and in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES
files.reason_for_vendoring: The header is compiled into the Gateway, so its revision is part of the module's binary identity. Distribution packages disagree (ubuntu:22.04 ships 3.10.5, the host carried a manually installed 3.11.3 owned by no dpkg package) and the inline ABI namespace introduced in 3.11 makes the generated code differ, which broke byte-level reproducibility between the host offline rebuild and the OCI image build (ISSUE-INF-001).
files.verification: infer-cpp/CMakeLists.txt verifies file(SHA256) against the registered digest at configure time and fails closed on drift; src/envelope.h additionally static_asserts NLOHMANN_JSON_VERSION_{MAJOR,MINOR,PATCH} == 3.11.3 so no system copy on the include path can win; scripts/run-supply-chain.sh re-verifies the digest.
files.update_policy: re-vendor only as an explicit revision change: update the digest in the registry, in CMakeLists.txt and in the compile-time assertion together, then re-run the supply-chain gate to confirm binary reproducibility still holds
files.exit_policy: replace with another qualified JSON library only together with a new envelope/config parsing qualification; the system package must never be used as an implicit substitute

method_allowlist.rationale: The upstream service definition also declares model-control and shared-memory RPCs. The Gateway wrapper never calls them and the Triton server runs with model-control-mode=none.
method_allowlist.enforcement: scripts/run-supply-chain.sh greps the Gateway sources for forbidden RPC symbols and fails the gate if any appears
